claims.text: As-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi nanoscale films and nanoribbons have high internal strain.
As-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi nanoscale films and nanoribbons have a fine-grained microstructure.
Intrinsic nanostructural stress broadens the magneto-structural phase transition and impedes the magnetocaloric effect.
High grain-boundary density broadens the magneto-structural phase transition and impedes the magnetocaloric effect.
Intrinsic stress and high grain-boundary density enhance magnetic hysteresis in the low-dimensional alloy.
Annealing in the proposed 300–400 °C range can relieve residual stresses in the FeMnNiGeSi films or nanoribbons.
The proposed annealing treatment can produce limited grain coarsening while preserving the low-dimensional geometry.
Residual stress, grain-boundary density, and local crystallographic anisotropy modulate magneto-structural coupling.
Changes in magneto-structural coupling control both magnetocaloric response and hysteresis.
Annealing makes the local strain distribution more homogeneous by relieving stress and increasing grain size.
A more homogeneous strain distribution sharpens the phase transition associated with the magnetocaloric effect.
Sharpening the phase transition reduces hysteresis under low-applied-field cycling.
Sharpening the phase transition produces a stronger and more efficient magnetocaloric response.
Relative to the as-deposited baseline, annealed samples will exhibit an increased adiabatic temperature change.
Relative to the as-deposited baseline, annealed samples will exhibit reduced magnetic hysteresis during low-field cycling.
The proposed improvement applies during magnetic-cooling cycles at fields up to approximately 1 T.
Annealing above the optimal temperature or for excessive durations can degrade the nanoscale structure.
Excessive annealing can cause unwanted phase coarsening that negates magnetocaloric benefits.
